auto_merge.commit_message:
This PR aims to resolve a few concurrency issues with the Cython cache
beyond what was reported in previous issues
(https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/7983 and https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/7985)
or fixed in https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8090 or https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/7986.
Here is a list of the fixes along with the failure modes that they avoid:

- **Isolate same-entry writers:** Give each process or thread its own
randomly named temporary file, created exclusively in the cache directory.
This prevents writers from truncating or interleaving each other's compressed data,
publishing an artifact another writer is still modifying, or renaming away the
temporary pathname another writer still needs.
This addresses the additional same-entry writer race noted in
https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/7983

- **Handle concurrent publication:** If Windows reports `FileExistsError`
because another writer already published the destination,
retain that entry and discard the caller's temporary rather than fail compilation.
Where rename replaces the destination, either complete artifact may win.

- **Clean up failed writes:** Attempt to remove the caller's temporary file
after compression or publication errors, including when another writer has
already published the destination, instead of leaving unfinished artifacts behind on failure.

- **Reclaim abandoned temporaries:** When cleanup scans the cache,
attempt to remove `.tmp` files whose last modification was more than one week ago,
while preserving recent temporary files.
Treat missing or inaccessible temporary files as best-effort cleanup failures.

Age-based cleanup is a conservative heuristic, not proof that a writer has exited:
a writer inactive for more than a week can still lose its temporary file.
The existing `du` fast path remains unchanged, so older temporaries may remain
while the cache is below its size limit.
An earlier iteration of the PR attempted to provide safe cleanup, but doing so
required a complex file locking scheme that we determined wasn't worthwhile,
see https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8108#issuecomment-6653082020.

body:
This PR aims to resolve a few concurrency issues with the Cython cache beyond what was reported in previous issues (#7983 and #7985) or fixed in #8090 or #7986. Here is a list of the fixes along with the failure modes that they avoid:

- **Isolate same-entry writers:** Give each process or thread its own randomly named temporary file, created exclusively in the cache directory. This prevents writers from truncating or interleaving each other's compressed data, publishing an artifact another writer is still modifying, or renaming away the temporary pathname another writer still needs. This addresses the additional same-entry writer race noted in #7983.

- **Handle concurrent publication:** If Windows reports `FileExistsError` because another writer already published the destination, retain that entry and discard the caller's temporary rather than fail compilation. Where rename replaces the destination, either complete artifact may win.

- **Clean up failed writes:** Attempt to remove the caller's temporary file after compression or publication errors, including when another writer has already published the destination, instead of leaving unfinished artifacts behind on failure.

- **Reclaim abandoned temporaries:** When cleanup scans the cache, attempt to remove `.tmp` files whose last modification was more than one week ago, while preserving recent temporary files. Treat missing or inaccessible temporary files as best-effort cleanup failures.

Age-based cleanup is a conservative heuristic, not proof that a writer has exited: a writer inactive for more than a week can still lose its temporary file. The existing `du` fast path remains unchanged, so older temporaries may remain while the cache is below its size limit. An earlier iteration of the PR attempted to provide safe cleanup, but doing so required a complex file locking scheme that we determined wasn't worthwhile, see https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8108#issuecomment-6653082020.

comment_data.body:
I wonder how much value this documentation adds (especially the description of temporary files). (i.e. is anyone going to change how they use Cython cache based on how this information?)

Maybe something like

> Cython cache is safe to use from multiple concurrent processes. Where multiple writers concurrent writers  conflict with each other, cleanup of temporary files can sometimes be deferred which costs a little bit of disk-space in the short-term.

Although even the last sentence isn't adding a huge amount.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -568,6 +568,13 @@ The Cython cache is disabled by default but can be enabled by the ``cache`` para
         ext_modules=cythonize(extensions, cache=True)
     )
 
+Concurrent cache writers use unique temporary files and publish only complete
+artifacts. When cleanup scans the cache, it removes temporary files whose last
+modification was more than one week ago. This age-based heuristic preserves
+recent writers' files but can remove a temporary file if its writer has been
+inactive for more than a week. Cleanup may skip the scan while the cache is
+below its size limit.

comment_data.body:
Personally I'd be inclined not to test boundary since it seems completely arbitrary either way and I doubt if we care if a future modification changes it from kept to not kept.

(But also since it's there maybe we don't care either way and should just leave it)

comment_data.body: I get the `preserves_reused_temporary` bit of this test, but I don't see how it's testing `publishes_complete_artifacts`. (In that it seems to me that this is tested too early?)

@@ -0,0 +1,189 @@
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
+import gzip
+import multiprocessing
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import stat
+import tempfile
+import threading
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+import zipfile
+
+from Cython.Build import Cache as cache_mod
+from Cython.Compiler.Main import CompilationResult
+
+
+STARTUP_TIMEOUT = 60
+OPERATION_TIMEOUT = 10
+
+
+def store_entry(cache_dir, source, header=None):
+    result = CompilationResult()
+    result.c_file = source
+    result.h_file = header
+    cache_mod.Cache(cache_dir).store_to_cache(source, 'key', result)
+
+
+def publish_entries(cache_dir, source, header, start=None):
+    os_open = os.open
+    threaded = start is None
+    if threaded:
+        start = threading.Barrier(2)
+
+    def overlapping_temporary(*args, **kwargs):
+        fd = os_open(*args, **kwargs)
+        try:
+            start.wait(STARTUP_TIMEOUT)
+            # Neither writer may publish before both have distinct temporary files.
+            if len(list(Path(cache_dir).glob('*.tmp'))) != 2:
+                raise AssertionError('writers did not create separate temporary files')
+            start.wait(STARTUP_TIMEOUT)
+        except BaseException:
+            os.close(fd)
+            raise
+        return fd
+
+    with mock.patch.object(cache_mod.os, 'open', overlapping_temporary):
+        if threaded:
+            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
+                futures = [pool.submit(store_entry, cache_dir, source, header) for _ in range(2)]
+                for future in futures:
+                    future.result(OPERATION_TIMEOUT)
+        else:
+            store_entry(cache_dir, source, header)
+
+
+def publish_with_group_permissions(cache_dir, source, header):
+    os.umask(0o002)
+    store_entry(cache_dir, source, header)
+
+
+class TestCyCacheConcurrency(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
+        self.root = Path(temporary.name)
+        self.cache_dir = self.root / 'cache'
+        self.source = self.root / 'module.c'
+        self.source.write_bytes(b'/* generated source */\n')
+        self.header = self.root / 'module.h'
+        self.header.write_bytes(b'/* generated header */\n')
+        self.cache = cache_mod.Cache(str(self.cache_dir))
+        self.context = multiprocessing.get_context('spawn')
+
+    def start_process(self, *args, target=publish_entries):
+        process = self.context.Process(target=target, args=args)
+        process.start()
+
+        def stop():
+            if process.is_alive():
+                process.kill()
+            process.join(OPERATION_TIMEOUT)
+            process.close()
+
+        self.addCleanup(stop)
+        return process
+
+    def join_process(self, process):
+        process.join(STARTUP_TIMEOUT)
+        self.assertFalse(process.is_alive(), 'cache writer did not finish')
+        self.assertEqual(process.exitcode, 0)
+
+    def assert_valid_artifact(self, path, zipped):
+        if zipped:
+            with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
+                self.assertEqual(sorted(archive.namelist()), ['module.c', 'module.h'])
+                for artifact in (self.source, self.header):
+                    self.assertEqual(archive.read(artifact.name), artifact.read_bytes())
+        else:
+            with gzip.open(path, 'rb') as artifact:
+                self.assertEqual(artifact.read(), self.source.read_bytes())
+
+    def check_publication(self, threaded):
+        for zipped in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(zipped=zipped):
+                self.cache_dir.rmdir()
+                args = (str(self.cache_dir), str(self.source), str(self.header) if zipped else None)
+                if threaded:
+                    processes = [self.start_process(*args)]
+                else:
+                    start = self.context.Barrier(2)
+                    processes = [self.start_process(*args, start) for _ in range(2)]
+                for process in processes:
+                    self.join_process(process)
+                cached = self.cache.lookup_cache(str(self.source), 'key')
+                self.assertIsNotNone(cached)
+                self.assert_valid_artifact(cached, zipped)
+                self.assertEqual(list(self.cache_dir.iterdir()), [Path(cached)])
+                Path(cached).unlink()
+
+    def test_concurrent_processes_publish_complete_artifacts(self):
+        self.check_publication(threaded=False)
+
+    def test_concurrent_threads_publish_complete_artifacts(self):
+        # A runtime deadlock must not prevent the parent from enforcing a timeout.
+        self.check_publication(threaded=True)
+
+    @unittest.skipUnless(os.name == 'posix', 'POSIX file permissions')
+    def test_published_entries_preserve_group_permissions(self):
+        for zipped in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(zipped=zipped):
+                writer = self.start_process(
+                    str(self.cache_dir), str(self.source), str(self.header) if zipped else None,
+                    target=publish_with_group_permissions)
+                self.join_process(writer)
+                cached = self.cache.lookup_cache(str(self.source), 'key')
+                self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE(os.stat(cached).st_mode), 0o664)
+                Path(cached).unlink()
+
+    def test_publishes_complete_artifacts_and_preserves_reused_temporary(self):
